parsed.explanation: Combined regime has no presentation imprisonment campaign, but has tier-1 exposures: federal birth-sex facility rule, birth-certificate school facilities binding visitors, document-discrepancy refusal with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility at entry, and documented custody harms including hormone removal and reported sexual abuse/forced labour. This state removed the only service-discrimination remedy and bars stronger local protections. Courts have blocked some orders and existing X passports remain valid, mitigating but not remedying operative rules. Net: below 0.45 universal-exclusion anchors, above 0.25 organised-targeting anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Document discrepancy can trigger refusal and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility; reports of passports confiscated/blocked; existing X passports valid only until expiration.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic; litigation challenging passport policy is pending.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry discrepancy can move traveller from screening into refusal/detention and custody exposures; home passport does not use domestic marker-change process.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National custody model includes conversion-therapy practices, hair cutting, hormone removal; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some national orders challenged/blocked; rescinded prison LGBTQ order is contested, but no documented effective remedy for custody practices.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention after entry or facility arrest exposes traveller to birth-sex system and removal of care; stopped reporting of trans prisoners reduces oversight.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federally funded single-sex facilities barred congruent with identity; this state's school rule requires birth-certificate facilities for everyone on school grounds including visitors.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No documented adult public-restroom ban outside schools in this state; 29 states plus capital have no mapped ban, but federal rule still applies.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: School rule is narrower than all-government-building bans but uniquely binds adult visitors; single-person option is written only as student guardian-consent accommodation.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care under 18; federal orders target minor care, investigate schools/teachers facilitating transition, and propose barring public insurance for under-18 trans patients.
care_services.protection: Several federal orders blocked/enjoined and proposed rules unresolved; adult care not documented as banned in this state.
care_services.interaction: Adult travelling with minor faces care-access uncertainty for minor and school-facility exposure; emergency care practice not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal policy defines sex as binary at birth, removes gender-ideology materials, frames radically pro-transgender groups as counterterrorism priorities; 2026 national risk assessment lists this state in worst group.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 2020 employment ruling and 2015 marriage ruling remain; courts have enjoined some orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing increases likelihood of strict document/facility enforcement; efficient institutions enforcing hostile rules are exposure, not mitigation.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor cannot use school facilities matching identity, only birth-certificate facilities or student single-person facility with guardian consent; under-18 care ban applies; teachers face prosecution for facilitating transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Guardian-consent single-person facility exists for students; some federal minor-care measures enjoined.
minors_guardians.interaction: Parent/guardian travelling with minor is covered on school grounds; seeking care or school access can trigger investigation/document scrutiny.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific homicide/violence figures documented; national bathroom-trespass arrest elsewhere shows criminal exposure where statute applies, with 24h men's-ward hold.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime law exists, but only 23 states cover gender identity in bias statutes and this state removed civil-rights protection in 2025.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Removal of state remedy means private service denial or harassment has no state ground for redress; violence counts are stated undercount floors and not used as rate.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Trans visitor refused service, housing or employment has no remedy under state law; 2026 law bars localities from stronger protections; custody and entry remedies not shown effective.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Federal litigation and injunctions partially operate; capital-city ordinance history shows local protection was pre-empted, not preserved.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper national protections do not cancel state removal or federal facility/document rules where no operative pre-emption is documented.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: unremedied birth-sex facility exposure and rejected complaints. This case is narrower on adult public facilities (schools/federal) but adds entry-fraud and custody harms, keeping it near 0.35 rather than above it.

Lower than 0.45-A: that anchor has all-government birth-sex bathrooms but ordinary emergency care and a prosecuted assault. Here custody hormone removal/sexual-abuse reports, counterterrorism framing, and state remedy removal add severity beyond a single facility rule.

Higher than 0.25-A: no documented recurring police raids, extortion, or imprisonment for presentation itself, and courts have blocked some measures. The exposures are institutional and legal rather than organised street targeting.

Materially lower than 0.65-A: that anchor has accepted documents, identity facilities, corrected refusals and convicted attackers. Here document refusal/fraud risk, birth-sex facilities, and removal of anti-discrimination remedy are operative and unremedied.

parsed.synthesis: Interaction is cumulative: a document discrepancy at entry can lead to refusal or fraud scrutiny, then detention where hormone removal and reported abuse are documented; in-state, the school birth-certificate rule binds visitors and the state has eliminated service-discrimination recourse while barring local restoration. Partial court injunctions, valid existing X passports, and absence of a documented adult bathroom ban or presentation-imprisonment campaign prevent a 0.25 rating. For minors, school facilities and under-18 care bans are the sharpest exposures. The harshest operative rules govern the traveller experience.
